fields.h1: Build a Surgery Consent Form That Arrives Signed on Surgery Day
fields.hero_description: Build a surgery consent form where staff fill in the case, patients e-sign at home, and each signed form saves to your database.
fields.features_heading: What the Surgical Team Gets With Each Consent
fields.features_subheading: Your hospital's legal and clinical teams write the wording. Emergent builds the surgery consent form and the record that holds it.
fields.feature_1:
Case details that staff fill in

Staff enter the procedure, the side, the surgeon, and the date before the link goes out. The patient reads those lines but cannot change them, so the record holds what staff typed.
fields.feature_2:
Approved wording, one section per screen

Paste the consent text exactly as your teams approved it. The form shows one section per screen, and the patient ticks a box under each section before the next one opens.
fields.feature_3:
Signatures from the patient and a witness

The app captures the patient's e-signature and, where your policy calls for one, a witness's e-signature too. Each one is stored with a printed name, the date, and the time.
fields.feature_4:
A list of who has not signed yet

Pick the hour, and the app emails your pre-op nurse every case on the next day's schedule that still has no signature. Each line on that list carries the patient's phone number.
fields.feature_5:
Patient or representative, on record

The first screen asks who is signing. When a parent, guardian, or other representative signs, the form also collects their full name, phone number, and relationship to the patient.
fields.feature_6:
Code a developer can take in-house

Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer can then host the form next to your patient portal, and every signed form stays in a database you own.

fields.usecase_heading: How Surgical Teams Put Consent Online
fields.tab_content_1:
No signature yet from 3 of Thursday's 22 patients

Marrowfield Surgery Center emails the consent link to every patient booked for surgery. Thursday has 22 cases on the schedule. At 2:00 PM on Wednesday, 19 of 22 are signed, and pre-op nurse Odette Rainsford gets an email listing the 3 patients who have not signed, each with a phone number to call.
fields.tab_content_2:
After staff fill it in, the procedure stays put

Imani Dellacroix, surgical coordinator at Tamarind Orthopedics, fills in the case first: right knee arthroscopy with Dr. Anselm Hartigan on Thursday, Nov 12. Wendell Ostrova sees those lines as read-only text, ticks each of the 4 sections, and e-signs. His record shows the procedure exactly as Imani typed it.
fields.tab_content_3:
Any unplanned step on Clementine waits for a call

Gullwing Animal Hospital asks every owner what the surgical team should do if something unplanned comes up. Rosalind Ferraby e-signs for her dog Clementine's spay and picks "Call me first" over "Proceed, then call." The Monday surgery board shows Call first and her number, 555-0142, next to Clementine.
fields.tab_content_4:
Who interpreted is part of Teodoro's consent

Teodoro Banuelos reads the Spanish wording that Ashby Point Medical Center approved for his surgery. Interpreter Graciela Montoya joins by phone, and the nurse enters her name and ID 2209 before the signature screen. Teodoro signs at 9:42 AM, and the interpreter's details save to the same consent record.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Surgery Consent Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to turn approved wording into a surgery consent form patients e-sign before the day of surgery.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Mark which fields belong to staff
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Pick the hour for the unsigned list
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start from the consent text your hospital already uses, as signed off by its legal and clinical reviewers. If the only copy is a scan, retype it exactly and proofread it against the original. Do not rewrite clinical or legal statements yourself; send any change back to those teams.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Go through the form and tag each line as staff or patient. Anything about the case itself belongs to staff and is entered before the link goes out. The patient's lines are the acknowledgments, the signer details, and the signature itself.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask your policy owner who may sign for a patient and whether a witness signature is part of your process. Each answer becomes a screen: a signer question, a representative's name and relationship, and a witness name with its own signature.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Choose when your pre-op nurse should see the cases that are still unsigned, such as 2:00 PM the day before surgery. Late afternoon leaves time to call each patient and resend the link before the schedule is final.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the approved wording and every field into one plain-English prompt, along with the signer rules and the alert time. Emergent builds the form and the table that stores each signed case. A later change is another prompt.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Connect it to your scheduling system
fields.howto_step_6_des: Link the app to the scheduling or practice software you already run, since the app can connect to any tool with an API. New cases can then arrive with the procedure and date filled in, ready for staff to check.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Fill in a sample case yourself
fields.howto_step_7_des: Enter a test case as staff, then sign it on your phone as the patient. Sign a second test as a representative. Confirm that the staff lines stay locked, the representative and witness fields save, and the 2:00 PM list shows any case left unsigned.

faq_plan.q: What is a surgery consent form?
faq_plan.a: A surgery consent form is the document a patient signs to record agreement to a specific operation. For hospitals that provide surgical services, 42 CFR 482.51 says a properly executed informed consent form for the operation must be in the patient's chart before surgery, except in emergencies.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a surgery consent form?
faq_plan.a: Gather the consent wording your reviewers signed off on and the case details staff will enter, then describe both to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English. Emergent builds the form and a table that holds every signed case. When the wording changes, describe the change and Emergent updates the form.

faq_plan.q: Can I turn my surgery consent form template into an online form?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Copy the approved text out of your current template, such as a surgery consent form PDF, and paste it into the prompt word for word. Emergent builds the form and its database from that prompt. Add the template's revision date as a field, so each signed record shows which wording the patient read.

faq_plan.q: Can a surgery consent form pull case details from the referral?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the referral arrives through a form or system the app can connect to. A referral form that saves the patient, the referring doctor, and the requested procedure as one row lets the consent start from that row instead of a retyped copy. Staff still confirm each detail before the link goes out.

faq_plan.q: Where should a signed surgery consent form be kept?
faq_plan.a: In the patient's medical record. For hospitals, 42 CFR 482.24 says all records must document, as appropriate, properly executed informed consent forms for procedures and treatments that the medical staff, or Federal or State law if applicable, specify as requiring written patient consent. The AMA Code of Medical Ethics also says a written consent form belongs in the record.

faq_plan.q: Can patients sign a surgery consent form on their phone?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The patient opens the link on any phone and signs with a finger after reading each section. The app captures that e-signature with the date and time. With Emergent, each signed form lands in a database you own. Ask your legal team whether e-signed consent fits your hospital's policies before you retire paper.

faq_plan.q: How long should a surgery consent form be?
faq_plan.a: As long as the approved wording requires, with nothing added around it. Cut fields the scheduling record already answers, and move pre-op instructions to a separate letter. A waxing consent form can fit on one screen, while a surgery consent form with several sections reads better as short screens with a progress count.

faq_plan.q: Can a surgery consent form include a witness signature?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add a witness step after the patient signs, where the witness types their name and signs on the same device or their own. The app stamps that signature with its own time, separate from the patient's. Your hospital's policy decides who may witness and when a witness is needed.

faq_plan.q: Can one surgery consent form template work for every procedure?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when only the case details change from one procedure to the next. Staff enter the procedure on each case, and the shared statements stay the same. When your reviewers write statements for one procedure only, add them as a section that appears just for that procedure, or keep a separate version.

faq_plan.q: Can a veterinary clinic use a surgery consent form for pets?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Swap the patient fields for the owner and the animal: the owner's name and phone number, then the pet's name and species. The signer screen asks for the owner, which is the main change from a tattoo consent form or any form clients sign for themselves. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing.

plan.angle: The top 10 is hospital and surgical center consent PDFs plus AORN, CHA and AMA guidance on the consent process: static sheets a patient signs once, with nothing behind them. This page shows the practice-side work around the form that those PDFs leave to paper: staff entering the case details before the link goes out, a list of unsigned consents the afternoon before surgery, a veterinary owner's call-first choice, and an interpreter recorded with the signature. The clinical and legal wording stays with the hospital's own teams; the page quotes only 42 CFR 482.51 and the AMA Code of Medical Ethics, with their limits, and never says the form makes consent valid.
